summary: Initial implementation kickoff between Redwood and Nightingale Freight to align on pilot scope, security requirements, networking, and success criteria. Customer leaning to Dedicated for latency-critical inference but wants security and VPC assurances before commit. Agreement to run a short pilot focusing on routing, KV cache priming and embedding throughput for search use case.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted economics and latency tradeoffs
Timeline and next steps for pilot
transcript:
Header: 2026-07-07 15:00 PT | Duration ~52 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM); Elena (Nightingale Head ML Ops), Derek (Platform Eng), Priya (CTO)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the account, with Luis our SE and Samir CSM. How's everyone?
[00:10] Elena Brooks: Hi, Elena here. We're excited to get this kickoff done, been looking forward to seeing performance.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya, CTO. We'll be mostly hands off but want to confirm security flow.
[00:20] Derek Chan: Derek, platform. I'll be doing the VPC work and firewall rules.
[00:28] Luis Ortega: Great, thanks. Goal for today is handshake: align pilot success criteria, networking, and what Redwood needs to get Duck — I mean, to get Nightingale up and running. Small typo from transcription: said "Duck" earlier.

[02:01] Maya: Quick commercial note, pilot typically runs 2–4 weeks depending on benchmarks. But let's talk goals: Elena, what's the highest priority?
[02:12] Elena: Latency is top. We run a parcels search that needs embeddings and re-ranking within our UI — target p95 < 200ms for document retrieval and re-rank, ideally lower. Cost matters but latency beats cost for this feature.
[02:26] Luis: Ok, p95 <200ms is reasonable if we run on Dedicated with GPU pools and keep KV cache hot. Two things we'll validate: cold start behavior and steady-state throughput.
[02:41] Derek: Our network constraints: private VPC in us-east-1, strict egress, no public peering. We can allow specific CIDRs for Redwood endpoints and do VPC peering/PrivateLink. Need details on exact IPs and port ranges.
[02:56] Samir: We'll provide the VPC peering doc. Also want to confirm retention — we don't want customer data stored outside the VPC.

[04:15] Luis: For Private and Dedicated modes, Redwood Private has options: private control plane or on-prem package. Slight transcription note: earlier I said "Redwood Private plane" which got garbled. For Nightingale, Dedicated with VPC peering should work: control plane in Redwood but data plane in your VPC.
[04:40] Priya: So control plane in Redwood, but can you guarantee no logs or payloads leave our VPC? We need KMS integration and HSM support ideally.
[04:54] Maya: Short answer: yes. We integrate with customer KMS and can do envelope encryption, and audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll send the exact KMS/HSM partners list in the security pack.

[06:10] Elena: Also SOC2, ISO stuff — we need the SOC2 report extract and the cert dates.
[06:18] Maya: We'll include SOC2 summary and the compliance binder.

[07:05] Derek: Regarding routing and failover, if Dedicated is saturated what happens? Can requests failover to hosted? We want graceful degradation.
[07:21] Luis: Yes, we support smart routing and automated fallbacks to compatible model variants and regions. In practice you'll pick a policy — prefer latency-first, or cost-first. For mission-critical flows you'd pick latency, and fallback to a slightly smaller model variant if capacity is constrained.

[08:50] Priya: Curious about model management — we have some internal fine-tuned checkpoints for re-ranking and ranking. Can Redwood host our custom model and pin versions?
[09:02] Luis: Yes, model versioning and rollouts are supported. We also provide quantization recommendations and can run A/B canaries. Note: small transcript glitch earlier where I said "rolls" as "roles".

[11:30] Elena: Our expected traffic: about 120 qps at peak, mostly embeddings + short generation for metadata. Embedding latency budget tighter. Any recommendations?
[11:40] Luis: For 120 qps, batching and KV cache are critical. We'll propose a batching configuration — continuous batching with dynamic batch size. Also recommend a small embedding GPU pool and dedicated throughput with autoscale headroom. We'll include a suggested configuration in the benchmark plan.

[13:15] Derek: Network setup: we need a list of egress IPs and a prescriptive security group list. We can't allow broad egress.
[13:25] Maya: Understood — we'll add CIDR and port ranges. For Private deployments we can also do PrivateLink.

[15:00] Samir: Onboarding runway: we usually schedule a pre-engagement for access (service account, keys), then a bench week, then pilot run. Typical timeline 3–6 weeks to have pilot metrics. Does that align with Nightingale timelines?
[15:16] Priya: We want a 4-week pilot and then executive review.
[15:22] Maya: Good, we'll aim for a 3–4 week pilot with weekly check-ins.

[17:00] Elena: A few security questions: will input data be redacted or masked by default? We process PII and some addresses.
[17:10] Luis: We don't alter payloads by default; redaction has to be applied upstream. But we can add tokenization hooks and recommend a transform pipeline. We'll document best practices.

[19:30] Derek: For metrics — what observability do we get out of the box? We need per-route latency, token cost, error traces, and audit logs.
[19:43] Samir: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks. We'll also ensure you can export to Datadog or Splunk.

[21:50] Elena: Can we run an initial smoke test with a subset of traffic so we don't impact production?
[21:58] Luis: Absolutely. We recommend a canary with 1–5% traffic then scale up. For the pilot we'll define canary windows.

[24:12] Derek: On the topic of benchmarks, can Redwood run an apples-to-apples against our current vendor? We use Vertex partly and some host model endpoints in-house.
[24:24] Luis: We can run comparative benchmarks — we'll ask for request traces and sample prompts, and we'll mirror them in the bench plan. Note: transcripts sometimes show "Vertex AI" as "Vertex aye" but it's the same.

[26:40] Priya: Cost: how will we estimate committed Dedicated capacity? We need a ballpark for monthly committed GPU hours.
[26:50] Maya: We'll produce an estimated cost model based on the benchmark run. For the pilot we won't require a full commit — just reserved for the pilot window with trial pricing. If you go to production we'll discuss reserved capacity contracts.

[29:15] Elena: Success criteria for pilot: p95 <200ms for embeddings/re-rank on production-ish traffic, <1% error rate, and consistent throughput at 100–120 qps for 30 minutes. Also security sign-off.
[29:30] Maya: We'll formalize those as the pilot's P0 metrics and put them in the runbook.

[31:02] Derek: Any constraints around SDKs? We use a Go microservice.
[31:10] Luis: We have REST and official SDKs for Python, Node, and Java; Go customers typically use REST or community Go SDK. We'll provide example snippets and a small Go wrapper if needed.

[33:40] Elena: Data residency: logs and metrics can remain in our region?
[33:47] Samir: Yes — metrics and telemetry can be forwarded to your region and your SIEM. We'll note that some control-plane telemetry may still be in Redwood's control plane region; we'll highlight in the security pack.

[36:00] Priya: SLA and escalation — who do we call if we see production P1?
[36:07] Maya: For pilot, we'll provide an on-call rotation and an escalation path. For Dedicated or Enterprise tiers we'll include SLA-backed targets.

[38:20] Derek: Anything we should prepare before the next hands-on?
[38:28] Luis: Share sample request traces, sample prompts, and a small dataset for embedding. Also set up a test VPC and grant a technical service account with least privilege to test peering.

[40:10] Elena: Timeline check: we'll share network artifacts by July 14. Pilot window target start July 20–24.
[40:20] Maya: That works. We'll target the week of July 20 for the dedicated demo and bench kickoff.

[42:55] Samir: I'll schedule weekly syncs and a Slack channel for real-time updates.

[45:00] Luis: Quick note on optimization: during the bench we'll test quantized variants for cost savings and routing policies to meet latency SLOs while reducing token spend. There was a small transcription hiccup earlier where "quant" became "count".

[47:15] Derek: One more on security: do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for our internal teams?
[47:23] Maya: Yes, SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported. We'll include onboarding steps for SSO in the runbook.

[49:05] Elena: Any blockers from Redwood side we should expect?
[49:12] Luis: Mainly time to provision dedicated GPU pools and coordinate network peering. We'll need the VPC details to finish.

[50:00] Maya: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + SOC2 by 7/9, Luis shares bench plan by 7/16, Derek shares network diagram by 7/14, Samir drafts runbook by 7/12. Pilot target week of 7/20. We set weekly syncs.

[50:40] Priya: Good, that matches. Thanks all.
[50:45] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

End of recording.
